candidates.name: QuantConnect Lean
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source algo-trading engine with a committed Data/option/usa/{daily,hour,minute,universes} sample-data tree (small sample tickers, zip-of-CSV format `YYYYMMDD_tickType_optionType.zip`) used for local backtests, plus a paid QuantConnect Data Explorer for full historical US options chains. The free sample is a handful of tickers/dates for testing, not a broad historical panel.
candidates.why_useful: Could serve as a template/format for point-in-time option-chain storage if the team ever builds its own ABNB options history; the sample data itself is too thin (few tickers) to use directly for ABNB implied-move backtests.
candidates.size_hint: sample only, unknown exact row count

candidates.name: Open Source Asset Pricing (Chen-Zimmermann) CrossSection
candidates.what_it_holds: Code (WRDS pull in Python, portfolio construction in R) reproducing 300+ published cross-sectional return anomalies, including an 'EarningsSurprise.csv' signal and (per the project's data portal) an Earnings Announcement Return / SUE-style anomaly among the documented signals. Pre-built signal and portfolio-return files are distributed off-repo at openassetpricing.com rather than committed in git.
candidates.why_useful: The EarningsSurprise / SUE-family signal underlying the classic earnings-drift anomaly is exactly the academic analogue of an 'earnings-drift dataset' — could be used to benchmark whether an ABNB-style earnings-drift effect is even a real base rate in the broader market before building any drift trade thesis.
candidates.size_hint: 300+ signals, decades of US cross-section, WRDS-derived

candidates.name: OIPD (options-implied-probability)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (354 stars, Apache-2.0) that fits an arbitrage-free implied-volatility surface from an options chain and converts it into a market-implied probability distribution for the underlying's future price; built-in free yfinance data connector; example notebooks pull GME options live.
candidates.why_useful: Directly usable as a method to build an ABNB earnings-implied-move / implied-distribution estimate from current Yahoo option chains (which the team already holds) ahead of the 5 Nov print — a ready-made implied-move calculator rather than data itself.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: uses the same Yahoo current-options-chain source already held; adds an implied-move METHOD on top, not new raw data

candidates.name: GammaGrid
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source dashboard (AGPL-3.0, 64 stars) computing dealer gamma exposure (GEX), max pain, open interest and an in-house-computed IV surface for a user's US-listed options watchlist, pulling from yfinance on a schedule; explicitly stores no historical dataset — users accumulate their own local history (~214 bytes/contract per snapshot) going forward only.
candidates.why_useful: Could be pointed at ABNB now and run through 5 Nov to build a homemade options-positioning/IV-surface time series into the print, but produces no retrospective history and duplicates the already-held Yahoo current-chain source.
candidates.size_hint: no committed data; per-snapshot local accumulation only
candidates.time_coverage: forward-only from whenever it is run
candidates.geography: US-listed options only (SPX/VIX index options excluded)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Yahoo current options chain already held

candidates.name: OptionMatrix
candidates.what_it_holds: GTK-based financial derivatives calculator implementing 171+ pricing models (Black-Scholes and many variants) for computing option prices, implied vol and greeks; 251 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Pure pricing/IV-calculation utility, not a data source; only marginally relevant as a fallback IV calculator if the team needs an offline pricer.

candidates.name: option_tools
candidates.what_it_holds: Python toolkit computing implied and historical volatility surfaces and greeks for Chinese ETF options (50ETF, CSI 300 ETF options), commodity and index options via Sina Finance data APIs; no committed historical data files, only sample plot images.
candidates.why_useful: Not US/ABNB relevant and no persisted dataset; noted only as a method pattern for building IV-surface visualizations, low value for this pitch.

candidates.name: py_vollib_vectorized
candidates.what_it_holds: Vectorized (numpy/pandas) implementation of py_vollib for computing implied volatility and greeks over full option chains at once; 161 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Utility for fast IV/greeks computation if the team assembles its own ABNB option-chain snapshots into a dataframe; not a data source itself.

candidates.name: VanillaOptionPricers
candidates.what_it_holds: Fast vectorized Black-Scholes-Merton and Bachelier option pricers and implied-volatility fitters (Python).
candidates.why_useful: Pricing/IV-fitting utility only; would need an actual ABNB option chain fed into it to be useful, no data of its own.
